security_audit.summary: The skill is legitimate Linear CLI documentation, and most static findings are false positives caused by visible markdown command examples. Real residual risks remain around API key handling, printing or deleting the Linear config file, broad temporary-file cleanup, and GraphQL examples that can expose workspace user email data.

remediation.issue: API key handling appears in setup and troubleshooting examples.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer interactive authentication or redacted environment setup. Warn users not to paste API keys into prompts, logs, shell history, or command-line flags.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting suggests printing and deleting the Linear config file.
remediation.suggestion: Replace raw cat and rm steps with redacted config inspection and confirmation-gated reset commands. State that config files may contain secrets.

remediation.issue: QA cleanup uses a broad /tmp/*.txt glob.
remediation.suggestion: Remove only files created by the QA workflow, such as /tmp/linear-qa-test.txt and /tmp/downloaded.txt, and avoid wildcard deletion.

remediation.issue: GraphQL examples query workspace user identity data including email addresses.
remediation.suggestion: Limit identity queries to required fields and explain that user or email listings should only be run with a legitimate workspace need.

- Defaults: `linear config set default_team_id TEAM_KEY`, `linear config set default_output json|tab
- Inspect or reset defaults: `linear config show`, `linear config unset default_output`

- **Sub-issues**: Set parent to associate related work (requires UUID: `linear issue update ENG-123
- **Scope creep**: Create separate issues for discovered work; link with blocks relation (`linear is

content.user_title: Manage Linear Work from Your AI Session
content.value_statement: Teams lose time switching between code and issue tracking. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through safe Linear CLI workflows for issues, projects, comments, attachments, and GraphQL queries.
actual_capabilities: Lists, searches, views, creates, updates, links, comments on, and archives Linear issues through documented CLI commands.
Lists, views, creates, updates, deletes, and assigns issues to Linear projects.
Runs Linear GraphQL queries and mutations when built-in CLI commands do not cover a workflow.
Documents authentication setup with Linear API keys and config defaults.
Explains attachment download, upload, and URL attachment workflows for Linear issues.
Provides QA and troubleshooting guidance for validating command behavior.
limitations: Requires the external linear CLI to be installed and authenticated before use.
Mutating commands can create, update, comment on, link, or archive real Linear data.
Raw GraphQL workflows require accurate UUIDs and knowledge of the Linear schema.
Attachment downloads and uploads can read or write local files when the user enables them.

use_cases.title: Triage assigned issues
use_cases.description: Review current Linear work, inspect issue details, and collect comments before starting implementation.

use_cases.title: Create and link delivery work
use_cases.description: Create parent and child issues, link blockers, assign ownership, and keep Linear aligned with code changes.

use_cases.title: Validate CLI documentation
use_cases.description: Run a structured QA checklist that confirms documented Linear commands match real CLI behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Show my current work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Linear skill to list my assigned issues for TEAM_KEY. Summarize the top items and ask before making any changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a new Linear issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Linear skill to create a Linear issue in TEAM_KEY titled "TITLE" with this description: DESCRIPTION. Confirm the team and content before using any mutation command.

prompt_templates.title: Link related implementation tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Linear skill to inspect ISSUE_A and ISSUE_B, then propose the correct relationship. If I approve, link them in Linear and show the result.

prompt_templates.title: Run an advanced GraphQL workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Linear GraphQL recipes to perform this Linear operation: OPERATION. Prefer built-in CLI commands first. If GraphQL is required, explain the query, variables, and local files before running it.

output_examples.input: List my Linear issues for the platform team.
output: Found open assigned issues for the selected team.
Grouped them by priority and state.
Recommended which issue to inspect first.

output_examples.input: Create a task and link it as blocked by ENG-123.
output: Prepared the issue title, team, and relationship.
Asked for confirmation before creating or linking work.
Returned the created issue identifier and relation summary after approval.

output_examples.input: Help debug a Linear GraphQL variable error.
output_examples.output: The skill explains whether an identifier or UUID is required, suggests commands to fetch the UUID, and points to the relevant schema reference.

best_practices: Confirm team, issue identifier, and mutation intent before using commands with --yes.
Prefer built-in Linear CLI commands before raw GraphQL recipes.
Use redacted authentication checks and avoid printing full API keys or config contents.
anti_patterns: Do not hard-code team IDs, project IDs, or issue UUIDs when the workspace can be queried.
Do not run destructive archive, delete, or reset commands without explicit user approval.
Do not paste API keys into prompts, logs, screenshots, or shell history.

faq.question: Does this skill install the Linear CLI?
faq.answer: It documents the install command, but the user or agent must run installation in the local environment.

faq.question: Can it modify real Linear issues?
faq.answer: Yes. Commands with creation, update, comment, link, project, or delete actions can change real workspace data.

faq.question: Does it need a Linear API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The Linear CLI must be authenticated with a configured API key or supported config before most commands work.

faq.question: Can it use raw GraphQL?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes GraphQL recipes for advanced operations that are not covered by built-in commands.

faq.question: Can it download attachments?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents commands that download Linear uploads to a selected directory or standard output.

faq.question: Is it safe for automated agents?
faq.answer: Use with review gates. Mutating commands, API key handling, file downloads, and GraphQL queries should require user confirmation.
